item.description: Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored (#29864) * Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored Multi-column (2 to 80 activation columns) mul_mat_vec_q for reordered K-quant and Q8_0 weights on the Intel XMX matrix engines (int8 DPAS, ESIMD), for the SYCL backend. It targets speculative decoding verification (2 to 8 tokens per step) and short prompt batches (9 to 80 tokens). Three types also use it for a single column (Q2_K, Q3_K, Q8_0). * Fixed regression bug real bug found: the first version produced NaN whenever the row count wasn't a multiple of 4 * Removed GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 activation * rewritten xmx_mul_mat 64-byte alignment and 16-byte pitch check on the activations * Implemented fused gate/up kernel One launch computes up * act(gate) for both FFN weights, reading the activations once and applying SWIGLU or GEGLU in the epilogue. It covers up to 16 columns and works for all six XMX types. * Removed the temporary XMX_NOGLU environment switch * Q2_K min-sum optimization Q2_K weight is d·scl·q − dmin·mc, where scl (the 4-bit scale) and mc (the 4-bit min code) apply to each half of a 32-weight group * Added dispatch check and GRF sweep tg128 on Q4_K_M goes from 26.67 to 28.23 tok/s on the B70 (+5.9%). Q6_K is unchanged. MUL_MAT passes 1727/1727 and MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION 1361/1361. Perplexity at batch 1 is 5.2064 with XMX and 5.2058 without. * Renamed variables * Added 2 environment variables GGML_SYCL_XMX_MAX_COLS (default 80, any value 0 or higher) and GGML_SYCL_XMX_GLU_MAX_COLS (default 16, range 0 to 16): the largest batch for the fused gate/up kernel. It is clamped to 16 because that is the most the fused kernel is compiled for, so the variable can only lower it. * Update esimd.hpp 1. All five quant structs were repeating the same boilerplate, so I moved it into shared pieces. 2. A new helper xmx_term does one DPAS, converts it to float and scales it per row. The four branches are now one or two lines each, and the shared Cb += z * d8r is written once. The refactor passes all three op tests. item.description: llama: create new fused op for QSA mask (#30640) * llama: create new fused op for QSA scoring * enroll glm5.3-next too * tests : initialize the remaining tensors in test_kpool_mask The harness sentinels were left uninitialized, so leftover memory could read as NaN and fail the NaN check. * ggml: generalize the k-pool mask op into ggml_top_k_mask The k-pool mask op only covered the pooled QSA selection of qwen4exp and glm5-next, while the DSA models and the DeepSeek V4 CSA build the same top-k mask by hand with fill, set_rows and add. ggml_top_k_mask(mask, top_k, score, blocks, extra) keeps the mask cells of the live picks and the extra cells, and sets the rest to -inf. Every row tensor is 4D in the layout of top_k, and the mask is broadcast to those rows, so a selection can also be made per head. score, blocks and extra are optional: without score every pick is live, without blocks a pick is a cell, and extra holds the cells a row keeps without a pick. llm_graph_context::build_fused_top_k_mask views the row tensors in the layout of kq_mask and registers the fused node. item.description: server: add realtime transcription API (#30636) * server: add realtime transcription API * drop transcription_sessions * proxy ws * add docs * server: let the API key middleware guard the websocket httplib runs the pre-routing handler before the websocket upgrade, so the API key middleware answers 401 at handshake like any other route. This covers the router proxy, whose children run keyless, and accepts the same key forms as HTTP (Bearer, raw key, X-Api-Key). * server: keep realtime slots out of the prompt loop A realtime slot waiting for audio is GENERATING with nothing to decode, so it fell through the prompt loop and took slot_batched. A request on a higher slot then failed can_batch_with on the task type and starved for the whole session. Realtime slots have no prompt: the loop sets them up once and always leaves them. * server: start the realtime session once its slot is live The audio stream was created in the prompt loop, which skips a slot that cannot batch with the one generating, and session.created went out before the task was posted: early appends failed and the reader quit, leaving the socket open and the slot held until the HTTP timeout. The slot now sets up its stream at launch and signals it with the begin result, session.created waits for it, and a reader that stops closes the socket so the session ends with it. * server: name the committed item in input_audio_buffer.committed Per the Realtime spec, item_id is the item made from the committed audio and previous_item_id the one committed before it, null for the first. committed now comes before the transcript that completes that item, and both go out with the item switch under one lock, so a delta cannot land between them. * server: use the GA transcription session shape The session object follows the GA Realtime schema: type transcription, with the input format, transcription model, turn detection and noise reduction under audio.input. item.description: ggml-cpu : select the NEON fp32->fp16 conversion (#30505) The __ARM_NEON branch defines both GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_* macros but selects only FP16_TO_FP32, so FP32_TO_FP16 falls through to the portable software conversion while neon_compute_fp32_to_fp16, a single fcvt, stays defined and referenced by nothing. __POWER9_VECTOR__ and __riscv_zfhmin select both. Add an #error pair that refuses a branch defining a COMPUTE macro without selecting it. That is how this stayed unnoticed: the fallback silently supplies a correct software implementation, so the only symptom is a hardware instruction nothing ever reaches. The FP16_TO_FP32 half carries a !defined(__F16C__) carve-out, because PR 30343 keeps that direction on the lookup table on purpose. item.description: tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise (#30818) * tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise The router scores are in the range 0, 1), so a random draw can leave the last expert (or expert group) still selected and the first one dropped tied within the noise between the backends. They then route a token to different experts and the logits differ by 4e-3 instead of the usual 5e-7. Beam is the only arch here with a real top-k (8 experts, 2 used) and a group top-k (4 groups, 2 used), so it is the only one that hits this: 2 of 20 seeds failed on an M2 Ultra, the other MoE archs select 2 of 2 and cannot tie. Fill the selection bias with a ramp of step 2 to give every expert a score range of its own, which turns the top-k into a function of the expert index alone. The bias affects only the selection, the weights still come from the unbiased probs, so the MoE output keeps its magnitude. Beam now matches the CPU reference within 4e-7 for all of 160 seeds. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : tell the CPU and the GPU of an Apple SoC apart in the device table Both devices report the same description ("Apple M2 Ultra" here), so the device column of the test table had two indistinguishable rows and a failing row did not say whether the Metal device or the host CPU produced it. Add the device name, which is also what -b takes, unless the description already is the name. item.description: server: add --connect, allow p2p access to server outside LAN (#28277) * init * wip * wire it up * make it clear that it's experimental * add props.connect_code * nits * fix windows build * server: do not advertise a connect code without the tunnel --connect-code on its own had no effect other than being served in /props, so the Web UI showed a remote access code that no tunnel was serving. Assisted-by: pi:GLM-5.3-Flash * ui : add the discover models components The Discover surface: the curated-catalog list with its search and skeletons, the details pane with its readme, metadata, Hub stats and download options, and the standalone download progress bar that replaces the plain one. The quant download button sizes its select with a new xs trigger, so the select gains that size and the muted box look. The store stays incomplete when a repo fails, so the next mount retries it. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : put the discover view in the models manager The manager dialog gains its second view: the Discover Models call to action fades the table out, slides the title with its compass mark, and fades the discover surface in; the arrow button returns to the table. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash # Conflicts: # tools/ui/src/lib/components/ui/button/button.svelte * ui : add the Enable Discover Models setting The flag gates browsing and downloading HuggingFace GGUF models, so it is declared on the discover layer; the repo-tree lookup in the manager layer above reads it from here. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : resume model downloads from the pause point A stopped download keeps its partial file instead of deleting it, so re-posting the tag resumes from disk. The first progress record now carries the resume offset, the paused snapshot survives into the resumed entry, and a pause settles as soon as it is requested. Assisted-by: pi * ui : lead the discover list with downloads The discover sidebar lists running downloads above the suggested models, and steps aside while a query is active. A paused download stays in the manager table, where it is resumed or dropped. Assisted-by: pi * ui : make resuming a paused download work Re-posting the tag of a paused download hit the router's "already exists" check, because a paused download parks its entry as DOWNLOADED until the next reload: a download entry that is not running is now replaced and resumed. The UI keeps the paused row when the request still fails, instead of dropping it and looking finished. Assisted-by: pi * ui : remember unfinished model downloads A partial file is named after its content hash, so nothing on disk says which model it belongs to once the router restarts. The router now keeps the tags of the downloads it started, clears a tag when the download finishes or is deleted, and lists what is left as still downloading without starting anything. The UI adopts those tags as paused on every list fetch, so a refresh or a fresh open shows an incomplete download and can resume it from the files already on disk. Assisted-by: pi * ui : show a paused download's state on its chip A paused quant chip reads as paused at rest, the way a running one shows its spinner, and offers the resume action on hover. The selector's download row gets a View in Discover action beside its cancel. Assisted-by: pi * ui : collapse the download options by default The copyable download command starts collapsed so the option rows lead; expanding it stays one click away. Assisted-by: pi * ui : keep decision models out of the hub lists Decision models answer with calibrated probabilities instead of text, so llama-ui cannot run them: the hub data layer drops them from the catalog and every search, keyed by the decision-model tag or a text-classification pipeline. Assisted-by: pi * ui : read download tags as quant and sidecar A : - tag now parses into its quant and sidecar instead of one opaque quant token, and ModelsService.draftSidecarsByRepo collects the router listing's sidecar-only entries per repo, replacing the inline copy in the models store. Assisted-by: pi * ui : cluster draft downloads under their main model Tracked downloads group by repo: the main weights lead and the draft sidecars ride inside their item as compact sub-lines, on the selector, the discover list and the manager table. The main model's controls pause, resume and cancel the whole cluster, and the manager's download rows select into the configuration pane. Assisted-by: pi * ui : act on tracked downloads from the table rows The table passes its clusters' draft sub-lines to the model rows. A row's actions cascade pause and resume, an in-flight row offers Cancel download while a paused one keeps Delete from disk, and the confirm dialog's copy follows the state. Assisted-by: pi * ui : give downloads a configuration pane of their own Selecting a tracked download opens the pane in a download mode: live progress with pause, resume and cancel, and See in Discover, instead of metadata and load actions that a model without files cannot offer. Assisted-by: pi * ui : make the discover details self-fetching and responsive ModelsDiscoverDetailsContainer owns the details, tree and readme fetches so hosts outside the discover view can render the pane, and the details layout adapts to narrow panes with container queries instead of viewport breakpoints. Assisted-by: pi * ui : download a matching draft with the main model A main quant download now pulls the quant-matched draft of the most preferred kind the repo ships (DFlash before MTP), fire-and-forget, so speculative decoding is ready when the main lands. Manual draft chips stay available; the options row also collapses to one column in narrow panes. Assisted-by: pi * ui : keep discover off by default and couple it with the hub setting Discover Models starts unchecked. Enabling it turns the Hugging Face Hub setting on and disabling it turns it back off, so the checkbox never lies; with discover off the hub setting stays available on its own for the display data. Stored and reset state are corrected the same way on load. Assisted-by: pi * ui : open the manage models dialog on the manager view The dialog now opens on the manager instead of returning to the last view, discover entries still land on the discover view while the setting allows it, and the discover surfaces follow the setting's state. Assisted-by: pi * ui : give the discover search room for its focus ring The sticky search bar insets from the panel edges so the focus ring stays inside the scroll container, and rows scroll behind an opaque bar instead of through it. Assisted-by: pi * common: settle sidecar names on the listing and drop unfinished partials An infix or trailing sidecar token is ambiguous: draft heads use it (Model-MTP-BF16.gguf), so do full models with embedded heads (Model-Q8D-MTP.gguf). Such a name is a sidecar only next to token-free main weights of the same family, while mmproj or imatrix anywhere in the name, or a leading token, decides alone (mmproj_f16.gguf). A quant tag always carries its bit count, so a sidecar named after no quant (mtp-Model-it.gguf) gets the bare tag: the listing, the plan and remove all use it. An imatrix tag resolves into a plan slot of its own, downloaded but never wired into the params. remove resolves the tag the way a download does and deletes the partial files of every planned blob, so cancelling a running download or dropping one left unfinished by an earlier run leaves nothing on disk. The router passes its token and releases its lock around the call, and records the unfinished downloads with an atomic write. llama download succeeds on a sidecar-only plan and prints its paths. * ui : move dialog views and draft states into enums and constants The models dialog's views become the ModelsDialogView enum, the draft subline's states join ModelRowDownloadState, the view fade and the copy-feedback reset move to ui constants, and the dialog's compass marks come from DISCOVER_ICON. Assisted-by: pi * ui : drop the unused discover surface The dead openDiscoverModels twin, the commented-out command divider, the details pane's unused onClose and its header's close button, and a redundant type cast leave; the command's copy feedback joins the shared reset constant. Assisted-by: pi * ui : trim the download option comments and highlight the chat template The comment verbosity the options panel and its chips carried shrinks to the non-obvious why, and the chat template dialog renders through SyntaxHighlightedCode as jinja instead of a plain pre block. Assisted-by: pi * common: only a .gguf file is a sidecar, and mmproj/imatrix as whole words A non-GGUF file named like a sidecar (quantization-mmproj-Q8_0.json) is picked as the mmproj, and a sidecar word inside a longer word of a model name (Phi-2-OmniMatrix.i1-Q4_K_M.gguf) drops the model. * ui: dedupe draft sidecar badges per quant The draft sidecar badges deduped by kind and repo without the quant, so with a draft cached at two quants only one badge survived, and a delete of the other main quant found no badge to remove its sidecar with. Also restores the getDownloadEntries doc lost when the clusters method landed above it. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: adopt the incomplete download status and drop the paused-ids registry The store inferred an unfinished download from a downloading entry it held no local state for, which misread a download running in another tab as paused and offered a resume the server rejects. The listing carries the "incomplete" status now, so the adoption keys off it directly. The paused ids no longer need to survive in localStorage: the server remembers them across restarts, and the progress snapshot was stale after a reload anyway. The stale localStorage key is removed. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: quant-match the pause and cancel cascades Pause, resume and cancel cascaded to every draft sidecar of the repo while delete only took the quant-matched ones, so canceling a Q4_0 download also killed a Q8_0 draft that belongs to another quant's main. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: collapse the duplicated draft subline markup The downloaded and in-flight branches repeated the identical connector, label and badge markup; one block with a conditional tail keeps the two states in sync. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: scrub positioned styles out of sanitized model card html The style attribute stays allowed for the KaTeX output, which let a third party card draw a fixed overlay over the app. The sanitize hook drops position:fixed and position:absolute values and leaves the KaTeX layout styles alone. item.description: tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test ran on were not a Muse Spark. Per-tensor rules lived inside the write path, where a flag picked the values of a tensor inside each of the two branches that store them, so a new rule meant a new flag threaded through both. The file asks to be rid of that in a TODO of its own. Give each rule a filler, pick one from a table keyed on a substring of the tensor name, and keep a single write path behind it. Mamba moves into the table and Muse Spark joins it: the gate filler draws the raw weight once per block and resolves alpha and beta the way the conversion does. Over a thousand seeds on a CPU build the worst case drops from 1.36e-05 to 2.48e-06 and the median from 4.10e-06 to 5.48e-07, with no seed above the threshold. The other 131 models come out identical to the bit, since no other architecture carries these tensors. ctest is green on a CPU build and on a CUDA build. * tests: draw every tensor filler from fill_normal The fillers repeated the generator and the distribution each time. The normal draw now takes its key and the other fillers transform its values, so the generator lives in one place. item.description: model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support (#30673) * model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support Kolibri-1 is a bilingual German/English MoE reasoning model with 78B parameters and 3.46B active per token: 50 layers, 384 routed experts plus one shared expert. Attention interleaves four sliding layers at a 513 window with one full layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE. GQA runs 48 query heads against 4 KV heads at head_dim 128 with a QK-RMSNorm, and every block carries four RMSNorms, so the attention and the MLP output are normalized before they rejoin the residual stream. Routing picks the experts from logits + expert_bias and weights them with the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, without renorm. The converter reuses AfmoeModel for the per-expert checkpoint layout and the expert selection bias, and writes the shared expert and the per layer sliding window pattern. The released FP8 checkpoint needs no special code, it goes through the generic weight_scale_inv path. Three tensor names are added to the mapping (post_attn_norm, post_ffn_norm, moe.router.expert_bias) and the 128k vocabulary registers the qwen2 pre-tokenizer by hash. The arch is registered in test-llama-archs, with GQA and the sliding window pattern.
